function_question: How does nature sense when the air gets damp?

opening.text: There was a girl called Noor who walked her little brother to school every morning.
Before they left, her brother asked the same question: "Do I need my raincoat?" And Noor was never quite sure.
He left his raincoat at home and came back soaked. Noor thought: "What if something could tell us, with no batteries, no screen and no phone?"

card.goal: Show when the air is damp

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: The soggy morning
chapters.line: Noor's brother drips by the door. She wants a weather helper that anyone can read at a glance.

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Noor asks for help
chapters.line: Noor has a question and a bright idea, but she needs a teammate. What about you?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: The weather feelers
chapters.line: You and Noor meet plants and animals that can feel damp air coming.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of two layers
chapters.line: The weather feelers share the secret they all use.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: Training in the pine cone lab
chapters.line: Noor finds two pine cones in the park and hands you one.

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: The idea storm
chapters.line: Smells, sounds, clouds: what changes when rain is coming?

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The plan
chapters.line: Every great weather flower starts as a drawing.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: The big test
chapters.line: The first petals barely move. You fix them, and try again.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: The weather flower
chapters.line: The petals curl, and Noor's brother grabs his raincoat.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Noor's brother never knows if he needs his raincoat, and Noor wants a helper with no batteries at all. Can you help her? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some engineers already have a spark of an idea. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature solved this millions of years ago. Tap each card to meet four nature heroes who can feel the damp!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which pine cone will be wider after an hour?
guide.sketch: Time to draw your weather flower like a real engineer!
guide.build_and_test: Build your weather flower and let's see how far its petals move!
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Change ONE thing and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Noor's brother checks YOUR weather flower every morning, and he hasn't been soaked once!

quick_check.question: In dry air the petal tip points to 10 mm. In damp air it points to 25 mm. How far did it move?
quick_check.right: Right! 25 − 10 = 15 mm. A big move means anyone can see the change at a glance.

clue_cards.name: Pine cone
clue_cards.trick: Each scale has two layers of fibres that swell differently in damp air.
clue_cards.does: Scales close in damp air and open in dry air, even on cones that fell years ago.

clue_cards.name: Wild wheat seed
clue_cards.trick: Two long bristles that bend as the air gets damp and dry.
clue_cards.does: Day after day, this rowing motion drills the seed into the soil.

clue_cards.name: Ice plant
clue_cards.trick: A seed capsule that opens only when wet.
clue_cards.does: Seeds come out when rain can wash them away and water them.

clue_cards.name: Frog
clue_cards.trick: Thin skin that loses water fast in dry air.
clue_cards.does: Many frogs are most active and loudest when the air is humid, often before rain.

predict.prompt: Swells or stays the same in damp air? Predict first!
predict.explain: Tissue and pine cone scales are hygroscopic: they soak up water from the air and swell. Glue one onto plastic and the pair must bend to fit.

lab.title: The pine cone lab
lab.predict: Which pine cone will be wider after an hour?

tool.name: Brainstorm
tool.intro: A brainstorm is a storm of ideas: first you make lots, then you choose. Today you'll use all 5 rules.

parts.name: Quantity
parts.what: Go for lots of ideas, fast.
parts.example: 🪥 20 toothbrush ideas in 5 minutes: tiny, glowing, musical…
parts.starter: Things that change when rain is coming: the smell, the clouds…

parts.name: No Judging
parts.what: Every idea is allowed for now.
parts.example: 🪥 "A toothbrush that sings" goes on the list too.
parts.starter: A funny one I'll still write down is…

parts.name: Wild ideas
parts.what: Say the wildest idea you can think of.
parts.example: 🪥 A toothbrush that brushes while you sleep.
parts.starter: My wildest rain detector would be…

parts.name: Build on ideas
parts.what: Take an idea and add to it to make it better.
parts.example: 🪥 "It sings" + "a timer" = it sings for 2 minutes.
parts.starter: The pine cone idea could get even better if…

parts.name: Pick the best
parts.what: Choose the idea that fits the goal best.
parts.example: 🪥 Pick the timer brush: it helps teeth the most.
parts.starter: The one I could turn into a sensor is…
